questions.stem:
The major product formed in the following reaction is
Compound (shown) —NaNH₂; Na, liq. NH₃→ major product
questions.solution: NaNH₂ first removes the acidic terminal ≡C–H, so that end is held as a sodium acetylide. An acetylide anion does not accept electrons from Na, so only the internal triple bond is reduced. Dissolving-metal reduction goes through a radical anion and a vinyl radical that prefer the trans geometry, giving an (E)-alkene. On workup the acetylide is protonated back, so the product is (E)-undec-7-en-1-yne (B).

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
Among the following, the conformation that corresponds to the most stable conformation of meso-butane-2,3-diol is
(Each option is a staggered Newman projection. One carbon carries the groups at top, lower-left and lower-right; the other carbon carries the groups at upper-left, upper-right and bottom.)

options.text: Newman projection — top: OH; upper-right: Me; lower-right: H; bottom: OH; lower-left: Me; upper-left: H
Newman projection — top: OH; upper-right: OH; lower-right: Me; bottom: Me; lower-left: H; upper-left: H
Newman projection — top: OH; upper-right: OH; lower-right: Me; bottom: H; lower-left: H; upper-left: Me
Newman projection — top: OH; upper-right: OH; lower-right: H; bottom: Me; lower-left: Me; upper-left: H

questions.solution: First check which projections are the meso isomer. Going counterclockwise, the two carbons show the same cyclic order of OH, Me and H in A and B, so these are meso. In C and D the order is opposite, so they are the chiral (±) diastereomer. A is the all-anti conformer. B keeps the two OH groups gauche, so an intramolecular O–H···O hydrogen bond can form, and this outweighs the gauche Me/Me strain. B is therefore the most stable meso conformer.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
For the following reaction scheme, percentage yields are given along the arrow:
Mg₂C₃ —H₂O→ P (4.0 g) —NaNH₂, MeI (75%)→ Q —red hot iron tube, 873 K (40%)→ R (x g)
P —Hg²⁺/H⁺, 333 K (100%)→ S —Ba(OH)₂, heat (80%)→ T —NaOCl (80%)→ U (y g) (decolourises Baeyer's reagent)
x g and y g are mass of R and U, respectively.
(Use: Molar mass (in g mol⁻¹) of H, C and O as 1, 12 and 16, respectively)
The value of x is ___.
questions.solution: Mg₂C₃ is hydrolysed to propyne P: 4.0 g ÷ 40 g mol⁻¹ = 0.10 mol. Deprotonation and methylation give but-2-yne Q, 0.075 mol at 75%. In a red-hot iron tube, three molecules of but-2-yne cyclise to hexamethylbenzene R (C₁₂H₁₈, 162 g mol⁻¹). That is 0.075/3 × 0.40 = 0.010 mol, so x = 1.62 g.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
For the following reaction scheme, percentage yields are given along the arrow:
Mg₂C₃ —H₂O→ P (4.0 g) —NaNH₂, MeI (75%)→ Q —red hot iron tube, 873 K (40%)→ R (x g)
P —Hg²⁺/H⁺, 333 K (100%)→ S —Ba(OH)₂, heat (80%)→ T —NaOCl (80%)→ U (y g) (decolourises Baeyer's reagent)
x g and y g are mass of R and U, respectively.
(Use: Molar mass (in g mol⁻¹) of H, C and O as 1, 12 and 16, respectively)
The value of y is ___.
questions.solution: Hydration of propyne (Hg²⁺/H⁺) gives acetone S, 0.10 mol. Ba(OH)₂ with heat brings about aldol condensation of two acetones to mesityl oxide T, (CH₃)₂C=CHCOCH₃: 0.05 × 0.80 = 0.040 mol. The haloform reaction with NaOCl turns the methyl ketone into 3-methylbut-2-enoic acid U, (CH₃)₂C=CHCOOH (100 g mol⁻¹). This acid still has a C=C, so it decolourises Baeyer's reagent. U = 0.040 × 0.80 = 0.032 mol, so y = 3.20 g.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
Given: D-Glucose —HNO₃→ P, [α]D = +52.7°
The compound(s), which on reaction with HNO₃ will give the product having degree of rotation, [α]D = −52.7° is(are)
questions.solution: HNO₃ oxidises both CHO and CH₂OH to COOH, so P is D-glucaric acid. The −52.7° product is its enantiomer, L-glucaric acid. L-Glucose (C), the mirror image of D-glucose, gives it directly. Both ends of the product are COOH, so a sugar whose diacid is L-glucaric acid turned end-for-end also works. D-Gulose (D) is such a sugar, so it gives L-glucaric acid too. A (D-mannose) gives mannaric acid, and B (L-gulose) gives D-glucaric acid (+52.7°).

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem: The reaction of Q with PhSNa yields an organic compound (major product) that gives positive Carius test on treatment with Na₂O₂ followed by addition of BaCl₂. The correct option(s) for Q is(are)
questions.solution: The test detects sulfur: Na₂O₂ oxidises S to sulfate, and BaCl₂ then precipitates white BaSO₄. So the product only needs to contain S. In A, the F is activated by o- and p-NO₂, so PhS⁻ substitutes it (SNAr) to give an aryl phenyl sulfide. In B, the soft thiolate displaces one nitro group, which is activated by the other meta-NO₂ and the I. C and D already carry SMe, so their products contain S whatever happens (in D, PhS⁻ simply displaces the benzylic Cl by SN2).

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem: The maximum number of possible isomers (including stereoisomers) which may be formed on mono-bromination of 1-methylcyclohex-1-ene using Br₂ and UV light is ___.
questions.solution: Substitution of an H at each sp³ carbon gives five products: 3-, 4-, 5- and 6-bromo-1-methylcyclohexene, each chiral (2 each = 8), plus achiral 1-(bromomethyl)cyclohexene (1). The allylic radicals are delocalised, so bromine can also attach at the far end. The C3 radical gives 3-bromo-3-methylcyclohexene (chiral, 2). The CH₃ radical gives 2-bromo-1-methylidenecyclohexane (chiral, 2). The C6 radical gives back 6-bromo-1-methylcyclohexene, so nothing new. Total = 8 + 1 + 2 + 2 = 13.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
In the reaction given below, the total number of atoms having sp² hybridization in the major product P is ___.
Compound (shown) —1. O₃ (excess) then Zn/H₂O; 2. NH₂OH (excess)→ P
questions.solution: Ozonolysis cleaves both tetrasubstituted C=C bonds of the central eight-membered ring. Each alkene carbon becomes a ketone, giving a 16-membered cyclic tetraketone. Excess NH₂OH turns all four C=O groups into C=N–OH. Each oxime has an sp² carbon and an sp² nitrogen. The O of N–OH is counted as sp³, so P has 4 + 4 = 8 sp² atoms.
